text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The leader of hardline Communist Refoundation party Fausto Bertinotti, opening the party's third national congress in Rome, repeated his support for the government but said such a support would be "critical and independent" (all).
* Fiat chairman Cesare Romiti, adding his weight to industry's criticism of the government, says Italy is living a "tragic moment" (all).

* The government has drafted an umbrella amendment to unify three decrees on broadcasting which should be approved before Christmas. The decrees include one which would extend broadcasting licenses due to expire at the end of January, which mainly concerns former prime minister and centre-right leader Silvio Berlusconi's Mediaset television group (all).

* The Cassation court, reopening one of the most controversial criminal cases in post-war Italy, ordered the retrial of Pietro Pacciani, an elderly farmer cleared of the "Monster of Florence" serial sex murders (all).
* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi from the Ecofin summit in Dublin said Italy's 1996 public deficit would be less than 140 trillion lire (all).
* Italian banking group San Paolo di Torino cut its prime rate by half a point to 9.5 percent and its top rate 1.5 percentage point to 16 percent (all).
* Industry minister Pier Luigi Bersani said the government would rapidly deploy incentives up to 10 trillion lire to boost industries facing flagging consumer demand (all).
* An economic survey shows 11.4 percent of Italian families think their income is not sufficient and 41 percent did not make any savings during 1996 (Corriere della Sera).

* In an interview Foreign minister Lamberto Dini says "Italy will not ask for a dilution of the Maastricht criteria...Europe must start only when the convergence process is really complete" (La Repubblica).
* Mediaset is said to have reached an agreement with Us group GTE and Norvegian company Telenor to launch a bid to become the third mobile phone operator in Italy (Sole 24 Ore).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
